extracted.intended_audience: research authors preparing and submitting manuscripts to Nature
extracted.subtask_description: Formatting and submission requirements and editorial expectations for contributions (especially Research Articles) submitted to Nature, covering structure, word counts, figures/tables, references, Methods, data/code statements, and editorial/production guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Article scope and novelty requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Articles are original reports whose conclusions represent a substantial advance in understanding of an important problem and have immediate, far-reaching implications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Articles are the main format for original research contributions to Nature; editors judge significance and suitability for a broad scientific readership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary paragraph (abstract-like) constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: Start with a fully referenced summary paragraph, ideally of no more than 200 words, separate from the main text and aimed at readers outside the discipline; avoid numbers, abbreviations, acronyms or measurements unless essential.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structure: 2–3 sentences basic-level introduction to the field; brief background and rationale; statement of main conclusions (introduced by 'Here we show' or equivalent); 2–3 sentences putting findings into general context. Refer to Nature's annotated example.

rubrics_metrics.name: Article print-length and typical word-count guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: In print, physical sciences papers do not normally exceed 6 pages on average, and biological, clinical and social-sciences papers do not normally exceed 8 pages on average; typical 6-page article with 4 modest display items ≈2500 words; typical 8-page article with 5–6 modest display items ≈4300 words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A ‘modest’ display item ≈ quarter page (~270 words). Composite figures that require half a page (~600 words) may require reduced text. Editors set final print length; authors may be asked to shorten papers exceeding limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference count guideline
rubrics_metrics.description: As a guideline, Articles typically have no more than 50 references in the main text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is no constraint on additional references associated with Methods or Supplementary Information; only one publication per reference number; additional references for Methods/SI are not included in main-text count.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subheading length limit
rubrics_metrics.description: Subheadings may be up to 40 characters (including spaces).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sections are separated with subheadings to aid navigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Word count exclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: Word counts refer to the text of the paper; title, author list, acknowledgements and references are not included in total word counts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this when budgeting manuscript length (body text only).

rubrics_metrics.name: Readability and audience accessibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Contributions should be written clearly and simply so they are accessible to readers in other disciplines and to readers for whom English is not their first language; technical jargon should be avoided or clearly explained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Titles and abstracts must be intelligible to any scientist; essential specialized terms explained concisely; non–native English speakers may consider peer review or professional editing but this is not a requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nomenclature and taxonomic requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: For gene, protein and other specialized names authors can use preferred terminology in current use but must give all known names at first use; Nature prefers internationally agreed nomenclature. New or revised formal taxonomic nomenclature for animals is accepted conditional on provision of LSIDs via ZooBank.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow community conventions and provide required identifiers (LSIDs) for taxonomic work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscript organization and required sequence
rubrics_metrics.description: Contributions should be organized in the sequence: title, authors, affiliations (plus present addresses), bold first paragraph, main text, main references, tables, figure legends, methods (including separate data and code availability statements), methods references, acknowledgements, funding statement, author contributions, competing interest declaration, additional information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For initial submissions, present manuscript text and figures together in a single file; include line numbers to facilitate review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formatting: spacing, language and spelling
rubrics_metrics.description: Contributions should be double-spaced and written in English (spellings as in the Oxford English Dictionary).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preferred format for text is Microsoft Word with style tags removed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial submission file format & presentation
rubrics_metrics.description: For initial submissions, encourage authors to present manuscript text and figures together in a single file (Microsoft Word or PDF, up to 30 MB). Figures may be inserted within the text at appropriate positions or grouped at the end; include line numbers within the text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Figures can be incorporated or supplied separately as JPEGs if unable to include them; initial submission figures should be good enough for referees but need not be production quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title length and content rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Titles do not exceed two lines in print (≈75 characters including spaces). Titles do not normally include numbers, acronyms, abbreviations or punctuation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Titles should include sufficient detail for indexing yet be general enough for readers outside the field to appreciate the topic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Text page and composition metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: An uninterrupted page of text contains about 1250 words; typical article compositions given as guidance for managing length and display item trade-offs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these metrics when estimating how figures/tables will affect allowable text length.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author contributions and equal-author notation
rubrics_metrics.description: Nature requires authors to specify the contribution made by their co-authors in the end notes; equal contributions may be identified by an asterisk with the caption 'These authors contributed equally to this work' immediately under the address list.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If more than three co-authors are equal in status, indicate this in the author contributions statement; present addresses appear immediately below the author list.

rubrics_metrics.name: TeX/LaTeX policy
rubrics_metrics.description: If the paper is prepared using TeX/LaTeX, Nature will need to convert this to Word after acceptance; all textual material should be included as a single .tex file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan for conversion and potential formatting changes after acceptance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Font and mathematical notation preferences
rubrics_metrics.description: Preferred use of a 'standard' font, preferably 12-point Times New Roman; for mathematical symbols, Greek letters and other special characters, use normal text or Symbol font; Word Equation Editor/MathType only for formulae that cannot be produced using normal text or Symbol font.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow these suggestions to minimize conversion and typesetting problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods section placement and purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: The Methods section is in the main text file, following the figure legends; it appears online but not in the printed issue and should contain all elements necessary to allow interpretation and replication of the results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Methods should be concise (typically not exceeding 3,000 words), subdivided by short bold headings, and should avoid repeating detailed methods already published (cite instead). Authors encouraged to deposit detailed protocols to protocol repositories (e.g., protocols.io).

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods structure and content details
rubrics_metrics.description: Methods should be subdivided into subsections referring to methods used, and inclusion of specific subsections for statistics, reagents and animal models is encouraged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If further references are included in Methods, their numbering should continue from the last reference number in the rest of the paper; Methods cannot contain figures or tables (use Extended Data or Supplementary Information as applicable).

rubrics_metrics.name: Data Availability and Code Availability statements
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide separate Data Availability and Code Availability statements after the main text statements and before the Extended Data legends; certain data types must be deposited in an appropriate public structured data depository with accession numbers provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Full access to deposited data is required at the time of publication; if full access is required for peer review, authors must provide it.

rubrics_metrics.name: References numbering and citation style
rubrics_metrics.description: References are each numbered, ordered sequentially as they appear in the text, tables, boxes, figure legends, Methods, Extended Data tables and Extended Data figure legends. When cited in the text, reference numbers are superscript, not in brackets unless they are likely to be confused with a superscript number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use linked fields from reference managers; use the one-click EndNote button to remove codes. Continue numbering through Methods and Extended Data. Only articles published/accepted or uploaded to recognized preprint servers should be in reference list.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference content and formatting rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Titles of all cited articles are required; titles are upright, first word capitalized, written exactly as in the work cited and ending with a full stop. Book titles italicized with capitalization of main words. Journal titles italic and abbreviated according to common usage. Volume numbers bold. Publisher and city required for books.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow Nature published papers as examples for detailed formatting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissible items in reference lists
rubrics_metrics.description: Only articles that have been published or accepted by a named publication, or uploaded to a recognized preprint server (e.g., arXiv, bioRxiv), should be in the reference list; published conference abstracts, numbered patents, recognized preprints, papers in press, and research datasets with DOIs may be included.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Papers in preparation should be mentioned in the text with full author list (or initials). Text, grant details and acknowledgements may not appear in reference list entries (with some exceptions for highlighted references).

rubrics_metrics.name: End notes and acknowledgements brevity
rubrics_metrics.description: End notes (including acknowledgements) should be brief and should not include thanks to anonymous referees and editors, inessential words, or effusive comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A person can be thanked for 'assistance' (not 'excellent assistance') or for 'comments' (not 'insightful comments'). Funding information for primary research should be declared in a separate funding statement and only if the work arose directly from the grant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competing interests declaration
rubrics_metrics.description: A competing interests statement is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include the competing interests declaration in the specified place in the manuscript end notes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional Information section content and order
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors should include statements at the end of the paper in the following order: Supplementary Information statement (if any), Correspondence and requests for materials statement (naming corresponding author), and other required lines; the corresponding author is expected to respond to enquiries and coordinate post-publication matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nature may publish peer review information (names of reviewers who agree to be cited) completed by staff during proofing; include reprints/permissions sentence if applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Life sciences and behavioural & social sciences reporting summary
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors of life sciences and behavioural & social sciences Articles must provide a completed Reporting Summary that will be made available to editors and reviewers during manuscript assessment; the Reporting Summary will be published with accepted manuscripts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Adobe Reader to open and fill these forms due to advanced features.

rubrics_metrics.name: Table formatting rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Tables should each be presented on a separate page, portrait orientation, upright on the page, not sideways. Tables have a short, one-line title in bold text and should be as small as possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define symbols and abbreviations immediately below the table, followed by essential descriptive material, all in double-spaced text. Use standard table formats where provided (e.g., cryo-EM, NMR, X-ray crystallography) and include as Extended Data where required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figure legend content and restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Each figure legend should begin with a brief title for the whole figure and continue with a short description of each panel and the symbols used. If the paper contains a Methods section, legends should not contain any details of methods. Legends should be fewer than 300 words each.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All error bars and statistics must be defined in the figure legend; present figure legends one after another in the text document for final accepted papers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figure simplicity and interdisciplinarity
rubrics_metrics.description: Figures should be as small and simple as is compatible with clarity; the goal is for figures to be comprehensible to readers in other or related disciplines and to assist their understanding of the paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid unnecessary figures and parts (panels). Data that can be stated briefly in text should not be converted to small figures or histograms that clutter the paper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figure panel rules and sizing
rubrics_metrics.description: Figures should not contain more than one panel unless the parts are logically connected; each panel of a multipart figure should be sized so the whole figure can be reduced and reproduced at the smallest size at which essential details are visible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nature standard figure sizes: 90 mm (single column) and 180 mm (double column); full page depth 170 mm. Composite figures occupying at least half a page may be equivalent to ~600 words of text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figure labelling, units and style
rubrics_metrics.description: Lettering in figures should be in lower-case type with the first letter capitalized and no full stop. Units should have a single space between the number and the unit, follow SI nomenclature or field conventions, and thousands should be separated by commas (1,000). Unusual units or abbreviations are defined in the legend.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use scale bars rather than magnification factors; avoid layering text directly over shaded/ textured areas and reversed type; provide keys to symbols in legends where possible rather than on the figure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figure file requirements and image integrity
rubrics_metrics.description: Nature requires figures in electronic format and that all digital images comply with the Nature journals’ policy on image integrity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow initial and revised submission guidelines for sizing, resolution and labelling; do not upload high-resolution publication-quality figures until requested after acceptance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figure quality and production timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Print-publication quality figures are large and are not helpful at submission; authors will be asked for high-quality figures when asked to submit the final version of their article for publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare production-quality figures only when requested; follow the production guidelines provided at that stage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Third-party rights for display items
rubrics_metrics.description: Nature discourages the use or adaptation of previously published display items (figures, tables, images, videos or text boxes); reuse may require rights that cannot be obtained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If necessary reuse occurs, Nature may contact authors to discuss sourcing alternative material; permissions and rights responsibility lies with authors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Colour figure charges and editorial discretion
rubrics_metrics.description: Nature Portfolio charges authors a fee for printing of colour figures to help cover additional costs; inability to pay will not prevent publication of colour figures judged essential by the editors but must be agreed with the editor prior to acceptance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact Nature offices for pricing and details; discuss essential colour usage with the editor if cost is an issue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extended Data purpose and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Extended Data figures and tables are online-only, peer-reviewed display items that provide essential background to the Article but are not included in print; a maximum of ten Extended Data display items is typically permitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extended Data tables formatted similarly to print tables but submitted as images (not editable Word) and not edited by subediting department. Extended Data legends listed at end of Word file. Refer to Extended Data items at appropriate points in main text. Encourage inclusion of simple schematic panels to summarize main findings when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementary Information (SI) scope and constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: Supplementary Information is online-only, peer-reviewed material essential background to the Article (e.g., large data sets, methods, calculations) but too large/unsuitable for print.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SI should not contain figures (additional figures belong in Extended Data); tables may be included only if unsuitable for Extended Data tables (e.g., large datasets best in Excel). Refer to discrete SI items at appropriate points in main manuscript.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chemical structures and compound characterization standards
rubrics_metrics.description: For guidelines on experimental methods and characterization of new compounds, follow Nature’s information sheet on characterization of chemical materials and the Nature Research Chemical Structures style guide.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the provided ChemDraw template and submit final files at 100% as .cdx files to minimize art/production changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registered Reports format
rubrics_metrics.description: Registered Reports are empirical articles testing confirmatory hypotheses where methods and proposed analyses are pre-registered and peer reviewed prior to research being conducted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult the Registered Reports page for further details and specific instructions for submission of this article type.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presubmission enquiry requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Presubmission enquiries via the online service must include a cover paragraph to the editor stating the interest to a broad scientific readership, a fully referenced summary paragraph, and a reference list.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this service if unsure whether an Article might be suitable for consideration by Nature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission requirements and publication policies agreement
rubrics_metrics.description: All contributions should be submitted online and all contributors must agree to all of Nature's publication policies before submitting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors must make data and materials publicly available upon publication and deposit data into relevant databases with public release by online publication date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial and subeditor intervention and final style control
rubrics_metrics.description: Nature's editors often suggest revised titles and rewrite summary paragraphs; after acceptance, subeditors ensure text and figures are readable and edit papers into Nature's house style. Nature reserves the right to make the final decision about matters of style and the size of figures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proofs are sent before publication; authors may discuss proposed changes but Nature has final say on style and figure sizing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Line numbers to facilitate peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: Include line numbers within the text to facilitate the review process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is specifically encouraged for initial submissions to help referees and editors reference parts of the manuscript.
